		→ Physically count the cash balance and verify with the records.  


### E. Liabilities 

Nature of Liabilities 
The liabilities include long term and short term loans, amounts due to suppliers, payables etc.  

**General Procedures** 
	→ The General steps for audit of liabilities include:
		✓ Verify the loan balances with the loan agreements
		✓ Ensure that the principal and interest are calculated and paid on due dates.
		✓ Check the ledger balances for the arithmetical accuracy.
		✓ Obtain the confirmation from the lenders and suppliers.  



## 14.3 AUDIT OF HOSPITALS

Hospitals may be incorporated as charitable institutions, government hospitals, private hospitals etc.

| 1. AOA / MOA                             | Study the AOA and MOA of the hospital to identify the objectives, powers and governance structure.                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2. Minutes                               | Read the Minutes to identify the significant decisions made and their impact on the financial statements.<br>For eg: Investments, Purchase of assets etc. |
| 3. Exemption Certificate                 | Examine the tax exemption certificate, if any, obtained from the Inland Revenue Department.                                                               |
| 4. Evaluation of Internal Control System | Obtain an understanding of Internal Control System and evaluate the operating effectiveness.                                                              |
| 5. Accounting Policies                   | Obtain an understanding of accounting policies.                                                                                                           |

### B. Audit of Receipts/ Incomes

1. **From Patients** 
Check the rates applicable for various medical facilities.
Check few invoices to ensure that the patients have been billed as per the appropriate rates.
Ensure that rent charges, medical consultancy and medicine charges are shown separately.
For any discounts issued, ensure that there is proper authorization.
Check the cash ledger and cross verify with receipts issued.  



 2. **From Grants | Examine the sanction letter**
Ensure that the grant has been properly classified and accounted for. (i.e. specific or general grant)
Ensure the compliance with the terms of sanction letter.  


3. **From Rent/Investment** 
Check the investment register/ rental agreement.
Vouch the dividend income/ rental income
Ensure the compliance with Income Tax Act for TDS.
Examine the bank account for receipts.  


4. **From canteen** 
If the hospital canteen is run by the hospital management itself:
Check the rate of food items
Check the daily sales register
Verify the cash receipts
Ensure that the income has been properly accounted for.  


### C. Audit of Expenses

 1. **Administrative Expenses** 
→ Examine the invoices and authorization.
→ For Salary and wages, check the computation, appropriateness of tax deduction and verify the payments.
→ For rent paid, examine the rent agreement and ensure proper booking of rentals.
→ If there is any abnormal expenditure, ensure proper disclosure.
→ Examine Bank/ Cash ledgers.
→ Examine the tax computation (or exemption if any)  



  2. **Visiting Doctors Fees** 
→ For visiting doctors, read the policy of payment and ensure that the payment has been made as per the policy.
→ Examine the acknowledgement of receipt of fees.  


### D. Assets and Liabilities

 1. **Assets** 
→ The assets of hospital consist of Medical Equipments, Furniture, Building, structure, stock of medicine and medical equipments etc.
→ Obtain schedule of assets
→ Conduct physical verification.
→ Conduct general procedure for verification (cost, authorization, valuation, depreciation etc)  



2. **Liabilities** 
→ Check the outstanding liabilities as on date.
→ For loans and borrowings, obtain the bank statements.
→ Obtain external confirmation for creditor’s balances.  |

## 14.4 AUDIT OF CINEMA HALL

### A. Understanding the Entity and Planning Activities

|  1. AOA / MOA | Study the AOA and MOA of the Cinema Hall to identify the objectives, powers and governance structure.  |
| --- | --- |
|  2. Regulations | Study the internal rules and regulations.  |
|  3. Minutes | Read the Minutes of the Board meetings to identify the significant decisions made and their impact on the financial statements. For eg: New Venture, Modernization of Hall etc.  |
|  4. Evaluation of Internal Control System | Obtain an understanding of Internal Control System and evaluate the operating effectiveness.  |
|  5. Accounting Policies | Obtain an understanding of accounting policies adopted by the Cinema Hall.  |
|  6. Industry Regulations | Obtain an understanding of cinema industry regulations and trends to identify the category of incomes, expenses, tax implications etc.  |



### B. Audit Of Receipts/ Incomes

1. **Income from ticket sales (Shows)** 
→ Ensure that entrance to the cinema-hall during show is only through printed tickets
→ Check whether the tickets are serially numbered and bound into books
→ Ensure that the number of tickets issued for each show and class are different though the numbers of the same class for the show on the same day, each week, run serially
→ Ensure that for advance booking a separate series of ticket is issued
→ Examine the internal controls over the custody of the stock of ticket
→ Verify that a proper record of ‘free passes’ is kept and that these are issued under proper authority.
→ Examine the daily collection register and tally with cash balance
→ Reconcile the amount of Entertainment Tax collected with the total number of tickets issued for each class.  


 2. **From Advertisements** 
→ Check the agreements with the customers.
→ Verify the charges collected for advertisements and compare it with the rates applicable.
→ Examine the cash/ bank ledgers for the payment received.  


 3. **Restaurant Income** 
→ Obtain an understanding whether the restaurant is run by cinema hall itself or let out.
→ Study the agreement with the tenant if the space has been let out
→ Study the internal controls over the food stuff.
→ Enquire about the arrangement for collection of the shares in the restaurant income.  

### C. Audit of Payments/ Expenses

 1. **Advertisements, Repair and Maintenance, Depreciation etc.** 
	→ Vouch the expenditure incurred on advertisement, repairs and maintenance.
	→ Ensure that no part of such expenditure is capitalized except the expenditure on extensive redecoration, and that should be adjusted as deferred revenue expenditure.
	→ Confirm that depreciation on machinery and furniture has been charged at an appropriate rate.  



 2. **Other Administrative Expenses**
	→ Examine the invoices and authorization.
	→ Verify the cash/ bank ledgers for the payments made
	→ For Salary and wages, check the computation, appropriateness of tax deduction and verify the payments.  


3. **Payments to Distributors**
	- Vouch payment on accounts of film hire with bills of distributors and in the process, the agreements concerned should be referred to.
	- Examine unadjusted balance out of advance paid to the distributors against film hire contracts to see that they are good and recoverable.
	- Enquire with the management if the advance money is not adjusted
	- Ensure that the provision has been made for advances that are considered irrecoverable.

### D. Assets and Liabilities

|                |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Assets      | - The assets of Cinema Hall normally comprise of fixtures, projectors, HVAC, Sound Systems etc. <br>- Verify the Cost, Authorization for purchase, Valuation, Existence relating to the assets. <br>- Check the inventory records for the existing assets. <br>- Obtain MRL regarding the ownership and valuation of the assets. |
| 2. Liabilities | - Verify the loans and borrowings by examining the agreements and minutes. <br>- For amount payable to distributors, examine the distributor's ledger accounts. <br>- Obtain external confirmation from the distributors.                                                                                                        |

## 14.5 AUDIT OF NGO
- A non-governmental organization (NGO) is any entity which has an objective of common interest of public.
- It is a non-profit entity that performs a variety of service and humanitarian functions of public welfare.
- Definition of NGO would include religious organizations, voluntary health and welfare agencies, charitable organizations, hospitals, old age homes, research foundations, etc. NGOs are registered under Institution Registration Act, 2034. The Social Welfare Council monitors the activities of such NGOs.
- Some of the NGO's in Nepal are CWIN (Child Workers in Nepal), Maiti Nepal - organization working against girl trafficking and women in exploitation, Transparency International - Nepal (TI-N) etc.

### A. Preliminary Activities

| 1. Registration        | Examine the registration documents of the NGO to ensure that the legal compliances has been met regarding the registration.                                                   |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2. Bye-laws            | Study the bye-laws, internal rules and regulations governing the NGO                                                                                                          |
| 3. Structure of NGO    | Review the NGOs Organization chart, Financial and Administrative Manuals, Project and program Guidelines, Funding Agencies Requirement and formats budgetary policies if any. |
| 4. Materiality Level   | Set the materiality levels for audit purposes.                                                                                                                                |
| 5. Tax Exemption       | Check whether the NGO has received Tax Exemption certificate from the Inland Revenue Department.                                                                              |
| 6. Accounting Policies | Obtain an understanding of accounting policies adopted by the hotel.                                                                                                          |




### B. Audit of Receipts/ Incomes

1. **Sources of Funds**
⇒ The main source of fund include grants and donations, fund raising programs, advertising, fees from the members, technical assistance fees / fee for services rendered, subscriptions, gifts, sale of produce or publications, etc.

2. **Contribution and Grants**
⇒ Study and examine the agreements with donor agencies.
⇒ Ensure that all the funds received have been accounted for.
⇒ Check that all foreign contribution receipts are deposited in the foreign contribution bank account as notified under the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 1976.  


  3. **Fund Raising Programs** 
⇒ Examine the authority to handle the receipts.
⇒ Ensure that collection are counted and deposited in the bank daily.
⇒ Verify the copies of receipts issued.  


  4. **Membership Fees** 
⇒ Check fees received with Membership Register.
⇒ Ensure proper Classification is made between entrance and annual fees and life membership fees.
⇒ Reconcile fees received with fees to be received during the year.  


  5. **Interest and Dividends** 
⇒ Check the interest and dividends received and receivable with investment held during year.  

### C. Audit of Payments/ Expenses

  1. **Project Expenses** 
⇒ Ensure that the project expenses have been incurred as per the objectives of NGO.
⇒ Ensure that the project and program expenses have been made as per the direction of the donor agencies.
⇒ Vouch the invoices and the payments made  


  2. **Administrative Expenses** 
→ Ensure that all the administrative expenses such as rent, office expenses, salaries etc. are properly accounted.
→ Examine the invoices and authorization for day to day expenses.  



### D. Audit of Assets

 1. **Fixed Assets** 
→ Verify the Cost, Authorization for purchase, Valuation, Existence relating to the assets.
→ Vouch all acquisition/sale or disposal of assets including depreciation and the authorization for the same.
→ Examine the donor’s letters/agreements for the grant.  



2. **Investments**
→ Check Investment Register and the investments physically ensuring that investment are in the name of the NGO.
→ Examine the new investments and their authorization.
→ Ensure that the income due on investments is properly accounted for.  


  3. **Cash in Hand** 
→ Check the cash book and ensure its arithmetical accuracy.
→ Conduct physical verification of cash balance.
→ For any difference, obtain reconciliation from the management.  


  4. **Bank Balance** 
→ Check the bank ledger and verify with the bank statements.
→ Examine the correctness of the bank reconciliations prepared by the management.  


  5. **Stock** 
→ Verify stock in hand.
→ Conduct physical verification wherever possible.
→ Obtain certificate from the management for the quantities and valuation of the same.  |

### E. Audit of Liabilities

 1. **Corpus Funds** 
→ Corpus fund refers to the capital of the organization.
→ It is a permanent fund generated and kept for the existence and sustenance of the organization.
→ Vouch the receipts by examining the letters from donors.
→ Examine the investment register for the interest income.  



 2. **Reserves** 
→ Vouch transfers from projects/programs with donor’s letters and board resolutions of NGO.
→ Enquire about special reserves created if any.
→ Check transfer of gross value of assets sold from capital reserve to general reserve and adjustments during the year.  


 3. **Ear-marked Funds** 
→ Earmarked funds constitute those funds which are set aside to pay for a specific project or event.
→ They are also known as “flagged” funds.
→ Check the requirements of donor’s institutions, board resolution of NGO, rules and regulation of the ear-marked funds.
→ Ensure whether such funds are properly disclosed and accounted.
→ If such funds are invested, ensure that the income from such investments is properly accounted.  

  4. **Loans** 
→ Study the terms and conditions of borrowings with the lender.
→ Vouch loans with loan agreements and the copies of receipts issued.  

## 14.6 AUDIT OF PARTNERSHIP

### A. Preliminary Activities


1. **Agreement**
Study the Partnership Agreement to identify the nature of business and terms and conditions of partnership.

2. **Contents of Partnership Agreement**
Identify important points such as:
✓ profit sharing ratio,
✓ capital contribution,
✓ extent of liability to be borne by the partners,
✓ borrowing powers of the partners,
✓ rate of interest on capital etc.  


 3. **Minutes** 
Study the minute book, for obtaining an understanding of the policy decision taken by partners relating to authorization of extraordinary and capital expenditure, raising of loans; purchase of assets, etc. 

 4. **Accounting Policies** 
Obtain an understanding of accounting policies adopted by the hotel.  

### B. Other Matters

| Compliance with objectives      | → Verify whether the business in which the partnership is engaged is authorized by the partnership agreement; or by any extension or modification thereof agreed to subsequently       |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Compliance with Partnership Act | → Ensure that the provisions of partnership act are duly complied with.<br>Note: Students may write the general provisions of the Partnership Act to make their answer more specific.  |
|                                 |                                                                                                                                                                                        |





### C. Financial Aspects

 1. **Incomes** 
⇒ Vouch the incomes from the various sources related to the partnership business.
⇒ Check the sales register and copies of invoices.
⇒ Examine the cash/ bank ledgers to trace the revenue.  


  2. **Expenses** 
⇒ Check the authorization for various expenses made for the business.
⇒ Verify the copies of invoice
⇒ Ensure that expenses are properly classified as capital and revenue expenses.  


 3. **Assets** 
⇒ Verify the Cost, Authorization for purchase, Valuation, Existence relating to the assets.
⇒ Ensure that assets of partnership are properly accounted and disclosed  


  4. **Liabilities** 
⇒ Examine the ledgers
⇒ Obtain external confirmation for the borrowings and material amounts.  


 5. **Advantages of Partnership Audit** 
	1. The audited account helps to settle the accounts between the partners which help to reduce the dispute between the partners.
	2. Audit helps the passive partners to check the moral of the managing partners whether they have taken any undue advantage from the partnership firm.
	3. Audited Accounts of Partnership Firm are necessary for computing the Taxable Income of Partners.
	4. Audited Financial Statement can be helpful in negotiation to admit a person as a Partner.
	5. An audited account is a reliable evidence for computing amounts due to retiring partner or representative of deceased partner.
	6. Audited accounts can be relied upon by Banks when advancing loans, purchase of the business, as evidence of the profitability of the Firm and its financial position.  


## 14.7 AUDIT OF CHARITABLE INSTITUTION

Charitable organizations are the nonprofit organizations (NPO) with the main objective religious, educational or other public interest activities that are philanthropic in nature.

### A. Preliminary Activities

|                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Constitution   | ⇒ Understand about the constitution of the Charitable Institution, (e.g. Trust, Society, etc.)<br>⇒ Examine the registration documents.                                                                                               |
| 2. Structure      | → Identify the powers of authorities with respect to investments, decision making and responsibility allocation.                                                                                                                      |
| 3. Activities     | → Ensure that the activities that are being carried on by the institution are in compliance with the objectives.                                                                                                                      |
| 4. Minute Books   | → Scrutinize the Minutes Books of the Managing Committee as regards various financial decisions including the decisions on sale or purchase of investments, Fixed Assets acquisition or disposal, receipt of Donation, Endowment etc. |
| 5. Internal Check | → Ensure that there is appropriate internal control system including an effective internal check system to prevent and detect the embezzlement and misappropriation.                                                                  |

### B. Audit of Incomes

 1. **Funds** 
→ Examine the vouchers and receipts with respect to the funds received.
→ Ensure whether the objectives in operating each fund have been fulfilled  


 2. **Donations and subscriptions** 
→ Vouch all donations received as shown in the cash book, with the counterfoil receipts.
→ In case of donation of assets or donations-in-kind, ensure that they are properly recorded.
→ Confirm whether there is an adequate control over unused receipt books;
→ Obtain all receipt books covering the period under review;
→ Test check the counterfoil with the cash book  

 3. **Investments** 
→ Ensure that all incomes from investments such as rent, interest and dividends are properly accounted for.  

  4. **Legacies** 
→ It is an amount of money or property left by someone in a will.
→ Examine the relevant documents relating to the legacies.
→ Ensure proper accounting and disclosure.  

 5. **Income Tax Refund**s 
→ Where income-tax has been deducted from the investment income, it should be seen that a refund thereof has been obtained since charitable institutions are exempt from payment of Income-tax.
→ Vouch the Income-tax refund with the correspondence with the income-tax Department; and
→ Check the calculation of the repayment of claims.
→ Ensure that the refunds have been properly accounted and disclosed.  



### C. Audit of Expenses

| 1. General Expenses | ⇒ Vouch the expenses with respect to authority, invoices and accounting.                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2. Tax              | ⇒ Verify whether the Institution enjoys income-tax exemption.<br>⇒ Examine whether the condition of exemption are strictly adhere to.<br>⇒ When tax has been deducted at source from Incomes like Rent, Interest, etc, see whether refund claim has been made.  |


### D. Assets and Liabilities

  1. **Assets** 
⇒ Obtain list of assets owned by the entity.
⇒ Verify the cost, valuation etc, with respect to the assets owned.
⇒ Check the investment register for the investments held by the entity.
⇒ Verify the cash and bank balances and check reconciliations for the differences noticed.  


 2. **Liabilities** 
⇒ Verify the Capital Fund and Other Liabilities, if any.
⇒ Obtain appropriate Management Representations and Certificates, in respect of the various aspects covered during the course of audit  

## 14.8 AUDIT OF PUBLISHING COMPANY

Publishing companies are those which are involved in the business of publishing the books, newspapers, periodicals etc.

 **A. Preliminary Activities** 
⇒ Study MOA and AOA to identify the objectives and powers of the authorities. Study the agreements made with major clients.
⇒ Obtain an understanding of industry regulations and trends with respect to the publishing business.  



 **B. Audit of Income** 
⇒ Examine the invoices to ascertain whether the Sales are properly accounted. For distribution of books/publications through distributors verify whether all sales have been properly recognized.
⇒ Ensure that the income from advertisement has been properly accounted for.
⇒ In case of individual contracts (one time contracts such as pamphlets, brochures publication), ensure that the income has been properly reflected.  


### C. Audit of Expenses 

**Production Account**
→ Examine whether a production account is maintained.
→ This account should be debited with the cost of copyright, paper, printing, binding blocks, editing, indexing, compiling, etc.

**Royalties**
→ Study the agreements made with the author.
→ Check royalties paid to authors and ensure that these are in accordance with the terms of agreements.
→ Ensuring that all royalties due but not paid, are duly taken into account.

**Discounts**
→ Ensure that the discounts allowed to agents are as per normal industry trends.

**Administrative Expenses**
→ Check the authority for expenses.
→ Ensure that all the expenses are supported by proper invoices.
→ Examine cash/ bank account to verify the payments.  



### D. Assets 

**General**
→ Ensure that all the printing equipments are properly accounted.
→ Verify the cost, authorization, existence etc. of the assets.
→ Ensure that the depreciation has been properly provided.
→ Obtain external confirmation from the debtors and receivable parties.

**Stock**
→ Verify that books consigned on sale or return are excluded from sale, but included in the closing stock.
→ Ensure that the closing stock of books on hand is properly valued according to the cost of production per volume.
→ Conduct physical verification for few items.  



### E. Liabilities 
→ Verify Share Capital, reserves & Surplus, Secured & Unsecured Loans of the Company.
→ Verify whether the form and manner of presentation of financial information conforms to accounting standards and applicable legal requirements
→ Obtain appropriate Management Representations and Certificates, in respect of the various aspects covered during the course of audit.
→ Examine if there are any disputes regarding copyrights and if so, proper provision has been made in the books of accounts.  


## 14.9 AUDIT OF CLUB
→ A club is an association of two or more people united by a common interest or goal.
→ The interest or the goal may be linked to hobbies and sports, social activities, political and religious views etc.

**A. Preliminary Activities** 
→ Examine the registration and incorporation of the club.
→ Understand about the objectives of the club and categories of the members.
→ Evaluate the internal controls over the receipts and payments.
→ Study the minutes and decisions of the authorities.  


### B. Audit of Incomes

**Membership and Subscription**
	→ Identify the rates of admission and membership.
	→ Vouch the receipt on account of entrance fees with members’ application.
	→ Examine the copies of receipts issued to the members.
	→ Vouch member’s subscriptions with the counterfoils of receipt issued to them.
	→ Cross check the cash ledger to trace the receipts.
	→ Ensure that arrears of subscriptions have been properly accounted and disclosed.
	→ Check the registration of members to ascertain the arrears of the member’s dues.
	→ Enquire whether necessary steps have been taken for the recovery of arrears.

**Sale of goods and services**
	→ The services may be in the nature of club facilities (gym, pool, sports etc.)
	→ Examine the rates applicable.
	→ Check the sales register and verify with the invoices issued.
	→ Verify the cash account to confirm the receipts.
	→ Ensure that such income has been properly accounted.  


### C. Audit of Expenses 

→ **General**
	→ Examine the authorization over the expenses.
	→ Check the copies of invoices.
	→ Ensure that the expenses have been properly classified.
	→ Vouch the various purchases within the objectives of the club such as sports items, furniture, crockery, etc.
	→ Vouch purchases of foodstuffs, cigars, wines, etc. and ensure that they are on normal market rates.

**Administrative**
	→ Check the calculation of salaries of the staffs.
	→ Ensure that the TDS has been properly accounted.
	→ Verify the acknowledgement receipts from the staffs.  


### D. Assets 
→ Obtain the list of stock of furniture, sports material and other assets.
→ Physically verify the items to ensure their existence.
→ Examine the investment register to verify the existence of investments. Ensure that all the investments are properly disclosed.  


### E. Liabilities 

→ Examine the suppliers account.
→ If required, obtain an external confirmation.
→ If there is any loan, examine the authority to borrow and compliance with the arrangements for borrowings.
→ Ensure that all the liabilities are properly accounted.  


## 14.10 AUDIT OF SMALL COMPANIES

→ Small business means privately owned and operated business which may include the partnerships, proprietorship, or an entity with very small number of employees.

→ In case of small business also, the auditor has to perform more or less the similar procedure as that of large business.

→ However, due to lack of segregation of duties in small business, there is a greater chance of misstatement in the financial statements. Therefore, the auditor has to assess the internal control system in more detailed manner.

### A. Preliminary Activities

|                            |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1. General                 | → Study the AOA and MOA of the entity to identify objectives, powers and scope of business activities                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 2. Internal Control System | → Study the internal control system adopted by the entity.<br>→ Evaluate the operating effectiveness of controls.<br>→ Ensure that the lack of segregation of duties is properly compensated by monitoring mechanism.<br>→ Enquire with the management regarding the various controls over cash handling, custody of stocks, accounting etc. |
 |

### B. Audit Procedures

 1. **Letter of Engagement** 
→ The auditor should submit the letter of engagement that defines the roles and responsibilities of the auditor and the management.
→ Auditor should receive the copy of such engagement letter as acknowledged by the management.
→ The letter should also explain the reliance which the auditors can place upon an effective system.  


 2. **Internal Controls** 
→ Auditor should report to the management, any defects identified in the internal control system through the letter of weakness.
→ The letter should also mention the suggestions for the improvement.  


3. **Sufficient Appropriate Evidence**
 → While vouching and verifying the transactions, the auditor should obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence about the authenticity of the transactions.


4. **Management Representations**
→ Before signing the auditor’s report, a letter of representation on the company’s letter head addressed to the auditors should be obtained.
→ The purpose of such letters is to place on record representation of management on significant matters affecting the account such as the ownership and basis of stating the amount of assets, liabilities, and contingent liabilities.
→ In addition, they act as remainder to management of their responsibilities.
→ Obtaining MRL, however, do not relieve the auditors of any of their responsibilities.  


5. **Reporting** 
→ If the financial statements are complete in all material respects show as to reflect the appropriate position of the business, the auditor may express an unqualified opinion.
→ Otherwise the auditor shall modify his opinion with appropriate reasons.  

## 14.11 AUDIT OF SOLE TRADER

→ Sole Trader is a person who is the exclusive owner of a business, entitled to keep all profits after taxes and also liable for all losses. Sole trader is also known as proprietor.

|  1. Requirement | → There is no legal obligation for a sole trader to get his accounts audited. However, the audit may be required due to regulatory requirements, such as on specific instructions of the bank approval of loans.  |
| --- | --- |
|  2. Discretion of the Sole Trader | → Sole trader can himself determine the scope of the audit as well as the conditions under which it will be carried out. He can also decide whether the audit shall be carried out continuously or at the end of the year.  |
|  3. Letter of Engagement | → The auditor should obtain a letter of appointment so that the responsibilities of the auditor and the trader are clearly defined. It will help to prevent misunderstanding in the future.  |
|  4. Audit Evidence | → Auditor shall verify the records kept by the trader and obtain sufficient evidence in order to form the opinion on the financial statements.  |
|  5. Audit Report | → Bases upon the results of evaluation of audit evidence, the auditor shall express an opinion on the financial statements.  |



## 14.12 AUDIT OF INCOMPLETE RECORDS

- Incomplete records is a situation where the informal accounting system is used by the entity instead of double-entry bookkeeping.
- For example a single-entry system may be used to maintain a reduced amount of information about its financial results.
- Other examples may include: Destruction of records due to fire or other natural calamities, Seizure of records by authorities like Excise, income tax, etc.

### A. Preliminary Activities

|  1. General Understanding | Obtain an understanding of the nature of the business and relevant industry trends of the business.  |
| --- | --- |
|  2. Internal Control System | Test the operating effectiveness of the internal control system.  |
|  3. Accounting system | Evaluate the accounting system adopted.  |
|  4. Limitation on scope | While evaluating the records, the auditor shall determine if there is limitation on scope.  |
|  5. Materiality | The auditor shall consider the concept of materiality and the audit risk involved with specific account balances and classes of transactions.  |

### B. Audit Procedures

| 1. Opening Balances             | Apply the principles laid down in NSA-510, “Initial Engagements – opening Balances” while verifying the figures of Opening Balances.<br>If the accounts are to be reconstructed, ensure that opening balances are verified from the previous year’s audited figures. |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2. Analytical review procedures | Apply analytical review procedures in depth on Balance Sheet and Profit & Loss items and investigate any fluctuations and variations.                                                                                                                                |
| 3. Assets and Liabilities       | Obtain external confirmations with regards to receivable and payable balances. <br>Conduct physical verification for the identifiable assets. <br>Obtain written representations for the disclosure of all material assets and liabilities.                          |
| 4. Cash Book                    | Examine the Cash Book/ Cash legder for various receipt and payments. <br>Trace the bank transactions with the Bank Statement and verify the bank reconciliation statement.                                                                                           |
| 5. Report                       | Form an opinion and issue the report based upon the evidences available.                                                                                                                                                                                             |


## 34.33 AUDITNG OF LEASING COMPANIES

- Lease is a written or implied contract where the owner of the asset (land, building, machinery etc.) grants the other party (lessee) the right to use its exclusive possession and use for a specific period and under specified conditions, for a specified consideration.

- Generally two types of lease are considered:
	a. **Finance Lease**: It is also known as Full Payout Lease. Here the lessor transfers substantially all the risks and rewards related to the asset to the lessee.
	Generally, the ownership is transferred to the lessee at the end of the economic life of the asset. Lease term is spread over the major part of the asset life.
	b. **Operating Lease**: Here the risk and rewards are not transferred completely to the lessee. The term of lease is very small compared to finance lease. Ownership along with its risks and rewards lies with the lessor. Here, lessor is not only acting as a financier but he also provides additional services required in the course of using the asset or equipment.

- Leasing companies facilitate the lease of various types of assets.

### A. Preliminary Activities

| 1. Compliance                    | 2. Check the compliance with regards to registration of leasing company and applicable acts.                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 3. Structure                     | 4. Obtain an understanding of the organizational structure of the entity by studying the AOA/ MOA and board minutes.                                                                                                                               |
| 3. Internal Control              | 5. Evaluate the internal control system for:<br>☑ Authorization of lease agreements,<br>☑ Receipts of lease rentals<br>☑ Follow up actions for lease payments<br>☑ Sanction of payments for day to day expenses and other administrative expenses. |
| 4. Accounting Policy and Records | 6. Obtain a list of books of account, documents and accounting policies adopted by the Company.                                                                                                                                                    |

### B. Examination of Lease Agreements

| 1. Identification of Parties and Asset | → Examine the lease proposal form submitted by the lessee requesting the lessor to provide him a lease the equipment → Examine the description of the lessor, the lessee, the asset under lease and the location where the asset is to be installed.                        |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2. Terms and conditions                | → Identify the nature of lease agreement as to whether it is a Finance Lease or Operating Lease and ensure the correctness of the accounting treatment in either case.<br>→ Note the amount and tenure of lease, dates of payment, late charges, deposits or advances, etc. |
| 3. Right of Sub-letting                | → Examine the stipulation as regard sub-letting rights, i.e. whether the agreement prohibits the lessee from assigning or sub-letting the equipment and authorities the lessor to do so.                                                                                    |
| 4. Specific requirements               | → Check whether specific terms and conditions prevail over the leased asset and whether such terms and conditions are specifically acknowledged by the parties.                                                                                                             |


### C. Appropriateness of accounting

| 1. Lease Rentals | → Ensure that the lease rentals are accounted as per the lease agreement and in compliance with accounting standard.                                                  |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2. Expenditures  | → Verify whether expenditure under various heads of account are properly authorized and sanctioned.                                                                   |
| 3. Provisions    | → Ascertain the adequacy of provision for bad and doubtful debts with reference to recovery of payments, litigations etc.                                             |
| 4. Insurance     | → Check whether the lease goods are insured and identify the terms and conditions of insurance agreement.<br>→ Check the regularity of payment if insurance premium.  |


### D. Procedures related to lease arrangement

|  1. Invoices | → Ensure that the invoice is retained in safe custody for the long term contracts.  |
| --- | --- |
|  2. Mode of payments | → Check the cash/ bank accounts for the lease rentals received.  |
|  3. Interest/ Delay charges | → Verify whether payment is received on the agreed dates, whether reminder are sent for overdue payments, whether penal charges, late payment charges, etc. are collected properly.  |

### E. Assets and Liabilities

 1. **Verification of Assets** 
→ Verify the cost, authorization for purchase, valuation etc. related to the fixed assets of the company.
→ Ensure that adequate depreciation is provided.
→ Verify investments made by the company and their appropriate disclosure and accounting.
→ Examine the debtors and receivables' accounts and compare with confirmations of balance received independently.
→ Examine the adequacy of provision of bad debts.  


2. **Verification of Liabilities** 
→ Verify the capital account.
→ Examine the accounts of sundry creditors and check whether there are any long outstanding dues. If so, enquire with the management.
→ Obtain confirmation from the suppliers and the creditors for material amounts.  


## 14.14 AUDIT OF HIRE PURCHASE COMPANIES

Hire purchase is the legal term for a contract, in which a purchaser agrees to pay for goods in parts or a percentage over a number of months. If the buyer defaults in paying the installments, the owner may repossess the goods.

Audit Procedures

### A. Preliminary Activities

 1. General Understanding 
→ Study AOA/MOA of the company to obtain general understanding and structure of the business.
→ Study the minutes and regulations.  


 2. Internal controls 
→ Evaluate the internal controls over:
✓ authorization of purchase of assets
✓ payments  


3. Accounting System 
→ Understand the nature of hire purchase transaction and the accounting treatment adopted by the client.  

### B. Hire Purchase Agreement

| 1. Written Form         | → Ensure that the hire purchase agreement is in writing and is signed by all parties.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2. Terms and Conditions | → Examine whether the hire purchase agreement specifies clearly.<br>✓ The hire purchase price of the goods to which the agreement relates;<br>✓ The cash price of the goods, that is to say, the price at which the goods may be purchased by the hirer for cash;<br>✓ The date on which the agreement shall be deemed to have commenced.<br>✓ The number of installments by which the hire-purchase price is to be paid, the amount of each of those installments, and the date, or the mode of determining the date, upon which it is payable, and the person to whom the place where it is payable; and<br>✓ The goods to which the agreement relates, in a manner sufficient to identify them.  |


### C. Incomes and Expenses

| 1. Hire Purchase installments | → Ensure that the installments are being received on regular basis.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2. Apportionment              | → Examine whether the installments are properly apportioned as Principal and Interest.                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| 3. Provision                  | → Check the adequacy of provision for doubtful debts                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| 4. Expenses                   | → Ensure that the expenses of the company are within its objectives.<br>→ Verify whether all the material expenses are properly sanctioned and authorized.<br>→ For administrative expenses such as salaries and wages, rent, etc., check the arithmetical accuracy and compliance with provisions of taxation. |



### D. Assets and Liabilities

 1. Assets 
→ Obtain the list of assets owned by the entity.
→ Verify the cost, authorization for purchase, valuation etc. related to the fixed assets of the company.
→ Ensure that adequate depreciation is provided.
→ Verify investments made by the company and their appropriate disclosure and accounting.
→ Obtain confirmation from the receivable parties.  


 2. Liabilities 
→ Examine the accounts of sundry creditors and check whether there are any long outstanding dues. If so, enquire with the management.
→ Obtain confirmation from the suppliers and the creditors for material amounts.  

## 14.15 AUDIT OF JOINT VENTURES (JV)

→ A joint venture (JV) is a business agreement in which the parties agree to develop, for a specific time, a new entity and new assets by contributing equity. They exercise control over the enterprise and consequently share revenues, expenses and assets. Generally, in a joint venture, both parties are equally invested in the project in terms of money, time, and effort to build on the original concept

→ The parties which enter into the agreement for the venture are known as co-venturers.

→ The benefits of joint venture arrangements are :
- ☑ To enable smaller companies to deliver large projects by combining their expertise and resources.
- ☑ To enable a larger company to acquire new resources or expertise from a smaller company.
- ☑ To enable a smaller company to benefit from the credibility and financial stability of a larger company.
- ☑ To gain local knowledge in overseas markets.
- ☑ To share risks and costs.


### A. Preliminary Activities

|  1. Agreement | Study the JV agreement to identify the project, the terms and conditions of the agreement and the partners.  |
| --- | --- |
|  2. Accounting Methods used | Identify the accounting policies and methods used for JV transactions.  |
|  3. Authority over the records | Identify the authority to keep the records of JV transactions and ensure that such authority has exercised its powers in compliance with the JV agreement.  |

### B.

### C. Audit Procedures

|  1. Accounting Records | → Examine the documents and accounting records of the joint venture.  |
| --- | --- |
|  2. Compliance | → Ensure that each and every transaction is in compliance with joint venture agreement.  |
|  3. Bank Guarantee | → Check whether the bank guarantee is obtained for the performance of the contract.  |
|  4. Retention Money | → If there is a provision for retention money, ensure that it is properly accounted.  |
|  5. Expenses | → Ensure that all the expenses of the project are properly recorded and are supported with the invoices and vouchers.  |
|  6. Disposal/ Takeover of assets | → Identify the assets used in joint venture and the arrangements regarding the takeover/ disposal of such assets.  |

## 14.16 AUDIT OF CO-OPERATIVE SOCITIES

→ Cooperatives are formed and in operation based on the mutual support and cooperativeness for the economic and social development of the general public consumers by the farmers, craftsperson (Kaligadh), class of people with low capital and low income, labors, landless and unemployed people or social workers of the country.

→ Provisions related to Audit of Co-operative societies as mentioned in Co-operatives Act, 2048

**Accounts – Sec 17** 
Section 17 of the Cooperatives Act provides that Accounts committee shall be formed and following duties shall be performed:
	(1) The general meeting of every association may elect and form one accounts committee consisting of three members including one coordinator.
	(2) The accounts committee may perform the internal audit of the association in a regular basis and give suggestions to the board.
	(3) The accounts committee has to submit its accounts related report to the general meeting  


**Audit of Accounts – Sec 37**
	(1) Every association or society has to get its accounts of every fiscal year examined by any registered auditor recognized by the Registrar or official designated by him/her within three months after the expiration of that fiscal year.
	(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in Sub-section (1), the general meeting of the concerned association or society may, with the approval of the Registrar, appoint a registered auditor and cause the accounts of that association or society to be examined by such auditor.
	(3) In appointing an auditor pursuant to Sub-section (2), the same person or company may not be appointed for more than three consecutive times.
	(4) A report on examination of accounts has to be submitted to the general meeting and got endorsed.
	(5) If the general meeting does not endorse the report on examination of accounts submitted to the general meeting pursuant to Sub-section (4), the general meeting may appoint another auditor and have an inquiry held or accounts reexamined.
	(6) The remuneration and facilities of auditor shall be as determined by the General Meeting.


**Duties of Auditor**
	→ Auditor shall ensure that:
		☑ The co-operative business has complied with the provisions of the act.
		☑ All the relevant regulations and directives applicable are complied with.
		☑ There is proper internal control system for custody and disposal of assets.
		☑ The administrative expenses are duly accounted and disclosed.
		☑ The general office expenses are supported by invoices and vouchers.
	→ Auditor shall obtain Written Representations and External confirmations wherever necessary.

# Chapter 15: GOVERNMENT AUDIT

## 15.1 MEANING

- Government is a system through which the affairs of the state are managed and directed for the benefit of the public at large. Government is expected to provide a transparent service with economy, efficiency and effectiveness to its citizens.

- The major source of revenue to the government is tax collection which may be in the form of direct tax such as income tax, indirect taxes such as VAT; Excise duty; Custom duty, exports, grants and donations etc. The government utilizes this income to declare the budget for national development and the fund is utilized in various ways to achieve the objective of national growth.

- Therefore, it is necessary to examine whether the amounts are properly used and any frauds or misappropriation is identified at earliest. The concept of government audit evolves here.

- Government audit is the systematic and professional examination of financial, administrative and other operations of a public entity.

- The UN handbook on government auditing defines government auditing as:

“The objective, systematic, professional and independent examination of financial, administrative and other operations of public entity, for the purpose of evaluating and verifying them, presenting a report containing comments, conclusion and recommendations and expressing the appropriate professional opinion in respect of financial statements.”

## 15.2 GOVERNMENT AUDIT IN NEPAL

### Responsibility of Government Audit 
⇒ The Office of the Auditor General Nepal (OAGN) is responsible for performing government audit in Nepal.
⇒ OAGN was established in on 2016/03/15 B.S after the appointment of Auditor General pursuant to the then constitution.  


### Recent Developments 
⇒ The Office of the Auditor General Nepal (OAGN), the Supreme Audit Institution of Nepal, is elected as member of the Governing Board of Asian Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions (ASOSAI) for a three-year-term of 2015–2018.  


### Auditor General Provisions stated in Constitution of Nepal Part-22 – Sec 240 

1) There shall be an Auditor General of Nepal.
2) The Auditor General shall be appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Constitutional Council.
3) The term of office of the Auditor General shall be six years from the date of appointment.
4) Notwithstanding anything contained in Clause (3), the office of the Auditor General shall be deemed vacant in the following circumstances:
	a) if she/he submits a written resignation to the President,
	b) if she/he attains the age of sixty-five,
	c) if a resolution of impeachment is passed against her/him as per Article 101,
	d) If she/he is removed by the President on the recommendation of Constitutional Council for being unable to discharge the duties of her/his office due to physical or mental illness, or
	e) if she/he dies.
5) Auditor General appointed as per Clause (2) shall not be re-appointed.

**Qualifications of Auditor General.**
6) Any person who possesses the following qualifications is eligible to be appointed as the Auditor General:
	a) holds a Bachelor’s Degree in Management, Commerce or Accounts from a recognized university, or has worked as a Special Class Officer of the Government of Nepal after successfully completing the Chartered Accountants examination, or has at least twenty years experience in the field of auditing,
	b) is not a member of any political party immediately before appointment,
	c) has attained forty-five years of age, and
	d) Possesses high moral character.

**Remuneration of Auditor General**
(7) The remuneration and conditions of service of the Auditor General shall be as determined by law.
The remuneration and other conditions of service of the Auditor General shall not, so long as she/he holds office, be altered to her/his disadvantage except in the case of declaration of a State of Emergency due to extreme economic breakdown.
(8) A person who has been the Auditor General shall not be eligible for appointment in other Government service.
→ Provided that, nothing in this Clause shall be a bar to appointment to any position of a political nature, or to any position which has the responsibility of making investigations, inquiries or findings on any subject, or to any position which has the responsibility of submitting advice, opinions or recommendations after carrying out studies or research on any subject.  



### Functions, duties and powers of the Auditor General Part-22 – Sec 240

 1) The accounts of the Office of the President and Vice-president, Supreme Court, the Federal Parliament, Provincial Assemblies, Provincial Governments, Constitutional bodies or their offices, courts, the Office of the Attorney General and the Nepal Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police as well as of all other government offices and courts shall be audited by the Auditor General in the manner determined by law, with due consideration given to the regularity, economy, efficiency, effectiveness and the propriety thereof.

2) The Auditor General shall be consulted in the matter of the appointment of auditors for carrying out the audit of any corporate body of which the Government of Nepal or Provincial Government owns more than fifty percent of the shares or assets. The Auditor General may also issue necessary directives setting forth the principles for carrying out the audit of such corporate bodies.

3) The Auditor General shall, at all times, have access to documents concerning the accounts for the purpose of carrying out the functions specified in Clause (1). It shall be the duty of the Head of the office in question to provide all documents or information which may be demanded by the Auditor General or her/his employees.

4) The accounts to be audited pursuant to Clause (1) shall, subject to the Federal law, be maintained in such form as is prescribed by the Auditor General.

5) In addition to the accounts of the offices referred to in Clause (1), the Federal law may also require that the accounts of any other office or institution be audited by the Auditor General.  |

✓ To encourage the practice of taking actions against delinquents and rewarding the excellent performers.
